stem: Which record set best supports comparing maturity observations over several days?
choices: Date, plant or location identity, representative canopy position, floral-development notes, and trichome observations
Date, planned harvest week, cultivar name, irrigation volume, and a single representative photograph from each observation day
Plant identity, room temperature, nutrient recipe, total days in flower, and the most mature trichome observation recorded that day
Date, canopy height, flower mass estimate, lighting schedule, and a summary maturity rating without retaining the sampled position
rationale: Repeated maturity assessment is strongest when observations are traceable to time, plant or location, sampling position, and the developmental indicators being compared.
